title.narrative: Integrated Primary health care emergency response to drought affected communities in Baidoa rural Bay region

description.narrative:
ltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="font-size: 8pt font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtAccording to the 2023 HRP, less than one third of the people in drought-affected areas are estimated to have access to essential health care. Reported cholera cases continue to rise compared to recent years. lt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 8pt font-family: Arial, sans-serif"gtFor example, in 2022, confirmed AWD/Cholera cases have increased by two-and half fold compared to 2021. The situation is bad in 2023 where from January to March 2023, an estimated 3,428 cumulative cases with 14 cumulative death (CFR 0.4%) have been reported. In 2022, measles cases have increased by three-fold. Since the start of 2023 and by end of March, more than 2,078 cases of measles have been reported by WHO, with 78% affecting children under-five, which indicates uninterrupted outbreak. Bay region is the worst affected for measles. Between January-March, it reported 742, the highest for any region in Somalia while more 206 cases of AWD/Cholera have been reported from Bay for the durationltspan style="color: red"gt.lt/spangtltspan style="color:black"gt Due to multiple risk factors and highly compromised nutritional status of children under 5, malnourished children are nine times more susceptible to morbidity. Since the start of 2021, Bakool region has accounted for more 38% of all measles cases reported from the combined five regions in South Somalia (MOH-WHO Week-19 Somalia Weekly EPI/POL Update). IDPs, both long-standing andlt/spangtlt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gtltfont face="Arial, sans-serif" color="#000000"gtltspan style="font-size: 8pt"gt newly displaced, as well as civilians in conflict-affected areas are among the most vulnerable, with many lacking access to essential basic services such as clean water, sanitation and primary health. Similarly, According to data obtained from the Somalia Health Cluster and WHO, there has also been a 63 percent decrease in reported measles cases across Somalia compared to the January-April average for 2016-2020, however Bay region was among the region with largest number of measles cases (≥99/100 cases) were reported in Bay (198 cases, while decline of AWD/cholera was reported by health cluster and WHO between January and April 2022,with indicative of 89% decline in AWD/cholera cases across Somalia compared to the January-April average for 2021 the largest number of AWD/cholera cases (≥100 cases) were reported in Bay with 256 cases, Baidoa district hosts high number of IDPs displaced from inaccessible areas of lt/spangtneighboringltspan style="font-size: 8pt"gt lt/spangtlt/fontgtltfont face="Arial, sans-serif" color="#000000"gtltspan style="font-size: 8pt"gt regions that have since increase the demands for enhanced primary healthcare services, this was also evident in HIDIG health facilities at ADC I in Baidoa town that recorded high number of children with suspected measles and AWD cases (HIDIG monthly reports: March, 2023), also, what contributes to the high morbidity in the area are recurrent shock, drought impact and conflict coupled with inaccessibility due to militia groups in Bay region resulting in IDPs, increased health care gaps specially child immunization and vitamin A supplementation, this coupled with limited number of free health services available are the main causes of the high number of consultations seen in our facility. High morbidity was particularly recorded among IDPs due to over-crowded shelter conditions which increase the risk of communicable and infectious diseases. In Baidoa district the situation continues to deteriorate due to the impact of the drought situation lt/spangtlt/fontgtltfont face="Arial, sans-serif" color="#000000"gtltspan style="font-size: 8pt"gt that has uprooted communities and destroyed their livelihoods. lt/spangtlt/fontgtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gt
ltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtIn response to the situation and needs elaborated above HIDIG is proposing provision of basic emergency health service delivery in Baidoa rural in one fixed health facilities and eight mobile team targeting drought and conflict affected population living in the target areas. HIDIG’s intervention means the provision of quality healthcare services including the provision of PHC supplies, BEmOC and CEmOC services, provision of routine immunization services to 0-12 months old infants including undertaking Measles and Polio vaccination campaigns to U5 children, ANC/PNC services for pregnant and lactating women, health education of expected women on danger signs during pregnancy and health education sessions on prevention lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgt
